title: How do people show respect to elders around the world?
examples: How do people greet elders in different countries?
Why do people touch elders' feet in India?

explain.say: Here is something amazing: almost every culture in the world has its own special way to show respect to older people. Look at the board. The first group is greetings.

draw.text: How do people show respect to elders around the world?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: How do people show respect to elders?

explain.say: In Japan, people bow. In the Philippines, children do the mano: they press an elder's hand to their forehead. In India, many touch an elder's feet, and Yoruba children in Nigeria may kneel or bow low. How do you greet elders?

draw.question: How do people show respect to elders?

explain.say: Now look at the meals group. In many homes, elders are served first, and everyone waits for the eldest to start. In Korea, young people pour drinks and pass things to elders with two hands. Which have you seen?

draw.question: How do people show respect to elders?

explain.say: The words group matters too. Many cultures use titles: Auntie and Uncle for older friends, polite word forms, or adding san after a name in Japan. Do you use special words for elders?

explain.say: So the ways are different, but the idea is the same everywhere: elders have lived longer and deserve kindness. Brilliant! Challenge: find out a respect custom from a classmate's culture.

faq.a: Mano po is a Filipino greeting where a younger person gently takes an elder's hand and presses it to their forehead to ask for a blessing and show respect.

faq.q: Why do people touch elders' feet in India?
faq.a: Touching an elder's feet, called pranam or charan sparsh, shows deep respect and asks for their blessing. The elder often touches the young person's head in return.

faq.q: Why do Koreans use two hands?
faq.a: In Korea, giving or receiving something, or pouring a drink, with two hands for an elder shows respect. Using one hand can seem too casual.
asks: Tell me about the At meals

faq.q: What does san mean in Japanese?
faq.a: San is a polite word added after someone's name, like Tanaka-san. Japanese has many polite word forms to show respect.

faq.q: How do Yoruba children greet elders?
faq.a: In Yoruba culture in Nigeria, boys traditionally lie down or bow low, called dobale, and girls kneel, called ikunle, to greet elders.

facts: In the Philippines, the mano gesture is a sign of respect to elders and a way of asking for their blessing.
In Yoruba culture, boys greet elders by prostrating (dobale) and girls by kneeling (ikunle).
In Korea, it is polite to give and receive things from elders with both hands.

quiz.say: What do respect customs around the world have in common?
quiz.why: Different actions, same idea: honouring older people.
